title: Pricing War Response
description: A competitor launches a free tier matching your core features. You have 2 weeks before the board meeting.

context.company: SaaS startup, $5M ARR, 45% gross margin, 18% annual churn, 50 employees
context.situation: Major competitor (public company, $500M ARR) just launched a free tier that matches 80% of your core features. Your largest customer (15% of revenue) is evaluating switching. Board meeting in 2 weeks.
context.time_pressure: Board meeting in 2 weeks. Need recommendation with financial impact analysis.
data_provided: Current P&L: $5M ARR, 45% GM, $1.2M S&M, $800k R&D, $600k G&A
Customer segments: Enterprise (60% ARR, 5% churn), SMB (40% ARR, 30% churn)
Competitor intel: Free tier has no SSO, no API, 5-user limit, no support
Switching cost analysis: Average 3-month implementation, data export gaps

stages.prompt: What framework(s) should you apply FIRST to diagnose this situation?

options.label: Porter's Five Forces + Competitive Response Matrix
options.rationale: Systematically analyzes competitive position and maps response options against rival's move

options.label: SWOT Analysis only
options.rationale: Too general. Doesn't provide actionable response framework for competitive threat

options.label: Immediate 20% price cut across the board
options.rationale: Reactive, destroys margins, signals weakness, no strategic framework applied

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Provide CEO-grade feedback on framework selection.

stages.prompt: Estimate the quarterly revenue impact if you lose 15% of Enterprise customers and 25% of SMB customers to the free tier. Show your work.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User estimated {response}. Correct: Enterprise $5M×60%×15%=$450k/qtr, SMB $5M×40%×25%=$500k/qtr. Total $950k/qtr ($3.8M ARR at risk). Evaluate their reasoning.
stages.sample_answer: Enterprise $5M×60%×15%=$450k/qtr, SMB $5M×40%×25%=$500k/qtr. Total $950k/qtr ($3.8M ARR at risk).

options.label: Differentiate: Launch 'Pro' tier with SSO, API, unlimited users, dedicated support at current price. Keep 'Starter' at $X. Invest in switching cost moats (integrations, data gravity).
options.rationale: Leverages competitor's free tier limitations. Protects Enterprise segment. Builds moats.

options.label: Match: Launch your own free tier. Hope to convert 5% to paid. Accept 30% revenue hit.
options.rationale: Race to bottom. Destroys unit economics. Hard to raise prices later. Signals commoditization.

options.label: Acquire: Buy a complementary tool to bundle. 6-month timeline. $2M cost.
options.rationale: Too slow for immediate threat. Integration risk. Good as secondary play, not primary response.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate strategic logic, financial impact, and execution risk.

stages.prompt: Draft the 2-slide board update: Slide 1 = Situation & Analysis. Slide 2 = Recommendation & Ask.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User drafted {response}. Evaluate clarity, data-driven argument, and board-ready framing.
stages.sample_answer: A good board update includes: 1) Situation summary with key data points, 2) Financial impact analysis with numbers, 3) Proposed response with rationale, 4) Specific ask from the board (approval, guidance, resources). Keep it concise — 2 slides maximum.

optimal.title: Strategic Differentiation Win
optimal.description: Launched Pro tier, retained 95% Enterprise, converted 10% SMB to paid. ARR grew to $6.2M in 6 months. Competitor's free tier became lead gen for you.

acceptable.title: Defensive Hold
acceptable.description: Price-matched selectively, lost 8% revenue short-term but stabilized. Slow bleed risk remains. Need product differentiation within 12 months.

failure.title: Value Destruction
failure.description: Panicked price cuts or free tier launch. Gross margin dropped to 25%. Burn rate unsustainable. Down round or shutdown within 18 months.

title: Acquisition Target Evaluation
description: Evaluate a $15M acquisition target for technology and team. Board needs your recommendation in 1 week.

context.company: Series B SaaS, $12M ARR, $30M cash, 80 employees
context.situation: Target: AI-powered analytics startup, $2M ARR, 15-person team (10 engineers, 3 PhDs), proprietary ML models for predictive analytics. Asking $15M (7.5x ARR). Your product lacks advanced analytics - this would fill a major gap and unlock Enterprise upsell.
context.time_pressure: Exclusivity expires in 1 week. Competitor also looking.
data_provided: Target financials: $2M ARR, 60% GM, $4M burn, 12mo runway, 120% NRR
Your financials: $12M ARR, 70% GM, $2M burn, 15mo runway
Synergy model: $3M ARR upsell in Year 1, $8M by Year 3. Cost synergies: $500k (infra, G&A)
Integration risk: Different tech stack (Python vs your Node), remote team in different timezone, key person risk (2 PhDs)
Comparable transactions: 5-10x ARR for AI/ML tuck-ins

stages.prompt: What financial frameworks are ESSENTIAL for this evaluation?

options.label: DCF + LBO + Synergy Quantification + Earnout Modeling
options.rationale: DCF for standalone value, LBO for leverage capacity, synergy model for strategic value, earnout for risk mitigation

options.label: Revenue multiple comparison only (7.5x vs 5-10x comps)
options.rationale: Ignores cash burn, integration costs, earnout structure, strategic option value

options.label: Gut feel + team assessment
options.rationale: Insufficient for $15M (50% of cash). Board will reject.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain why comprehensive financial modeling is non-negotiable.

stages.prompt: Build the synergy model: Calculate Year 1 combined FCF impact. Assume: Your FCF = $2M. Target FCF = -$2M (burn). Revenue synergies = $3M ARR at 70% GM. Cost synergies = $500k. Integration costs = $1M one-time. Show Year 1 FCF.
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User calculated {response}. Correct: $2M + (-$2M) + $2.1M (synergy GP) + $0.5M - $1M = $1.6M combined FCF vs $2M standalone. Dilutive Year 1, accretive Year 2+. Evaluate.
stages.sample_answer: $2M + (-$2M) + $2.1M (synergy GP) + $0.5M - $1M = $1.6M combined FCF vs $2M standalone. Dilutive Year 1, accretive Year 2+.

stages.prompt: Structure the deal. Choose the best structure:

options.label: $10M cash at close + $5M earnout over 2 years tied to ARR milestones ($3M Y1, $8M Y3) + 2-year retention packages for 3 key people
options.rationale: Aligns incentives, mitigates key person risk, pays for performance, preserves cash

options.label: $15M all cash at close. Clean and simple.
options.rationale: 50% of cash gone. No protection if team leaves or tech doesn't integrate. All risk on buyer.

options.label: $5M cash + $10M stock. Shares risk.
options.rationale: Better cash preservation but complex valuation, tax issues, misaligned if stock drops

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate risk allocation, incentive alignment, and cash preservation.

optimal.title: Successful Tuck-in
optimal.description: Earnout achieved. Analytics module launched in 4 months. Enterprise upsell $4M ARR Year 1. Team retained. ROIC > 25% by Year 2.

acceptable.title: Partial Success
acceptable.description: Tech integrated in 8 months (slower). Only 1 PhD stayed. Upsell $2M Year 1. Break-even Year 3. Distraction from core product.

failure.title: Failed Integration
failure.description: Both PhDs left at 12 months. Tech debt unmaintainable. $15M write-down. Enterprise deals lost due to distraction. Cash crisis.

title: Crisis: Major Security Incident
description: Data breach affecting 10,000 customers. 4 hours since discovery. Regulators, customers, board all need communication.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $20M ARR, SOC2 certified, 150 employees
context.situation: Unauthorized access to customer PII database discovered 4 hours ago. ~10,000 records exposed (names, emails, company info - no passwords/financials). Attack vector: compromised contractor credentials. Contained 1 hour ago. Legal says 72-hour notification clock started.
context.time_pressure: 72 hours for regulatory notification. Customers expecting update NOW. Board emergency call in 2 hours.
data_provided: Incident timeline: Detection → Containment → Investigation status
Data scope: 10,000 records, PII categories, no auth/financial data
Root cause (preliminary): Contractor MFA bypass via session hijacking
Regulatory: GDPR (EU customers), CCPA (CA), industry-specific
Customer impact: 3 Enterprise accounts (€2M ARR) in affected set

stages.prompt: First 30 minutes: What are your IMMEDIATE priorities? (Select top 3)

options.label: 1) Confirm containment 2) Activate incident response team 3) Preserve evidence for forensics
options.rationale: Correct priority order: stop bleeding, mobilize, preserve legal position

options.label: 1) Draft customer email 2) Call lawyer 3) Post on Twitter transparency
options.rationale: Communication before containment = misinformation risk. Evidence preservation critical for liability.

options.label: 1) Blame contractor 2) Minimize scope in internal comms 3) Delay notification
options.rationale: Destroys trust, legal exposure, regulatory violations. Career-ending for CEO.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain crisis management priority framework.

stages.prompt: Board call in 30 min. What's your recommendation on customer notification timing?

options.label: Notify affected customers within 24 hours with: what happened, what data, what we're doing, what they should do, dedicated support line
options.rationale: Exceeds regulatory minimum. Builds trust. Controls narrative. Reduces legal liability.

options.label: Wait for full forensic report (5-7 days) then notify
options.rationale: Violates GDPR 72-hour rule. Looks like cover-up. Increases fines 4x. Destroys customer trust.

options.label: Notify only the 3 Enterprise accounts. Keep quiet on others.
options.rationale: Discriminatory notification. Regulatory violation. Leaks inevitable. Reputation destroys company.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain regulatory requirements and trust economics.

optimal.title: Trust Strengthened
optimal.description: Transparent, fast response. Customers appreciate honesty. 0 churn from incident. SOC2 renewed with commendation. Industry case study for crisis done right.

acceptable.title: Managed Crisis
acceptable.description: Met regulatory minimums. Some customer frustration. 2% churn. $200k fines. Reputation recoverable in 12 months.

failure.title: Existential Crisis
failure.description: Delayed/partial notification. GDPR fine €4M. Class action lawsuit. 3 Enterprise accounts churn. Board loses confidence. CEO replaced.

title: Scaling Org from 50 to 200
description: Your startup just raised Series B. You need to double the team in 6 months while maintaining culture and performance.

context.company: Series B SaaS, $8M ARR, 50 employees, remote-first since seed
context.situation: Just closed $20M Series B. Board expects 200 headcount in 18 months. Current: 3-layer org, 5-person leadership team. Culture: high-autonomy, written-first, transparent. Key risk: two key engineers (15-person team managers) showing burnout signs. VP Sales search has failed twice (3 months).
context.time_pressure: Q1 hiring plan due in 2 weeks. All-hands on Friday expecting culture message.
data_provided: Current org chart (3 layers: CEO > 5 leaders > 45 ICs)
Hiring pipeline: 8 open roles, 3 offers out, 2 week average to fill
Engagement survey: 82 eNPS, declining trend
Burnout indicators: 2 managers working weekends, productivity down 15%
Competing offers: 3 engineers received 30%+ salary bumps from FAANG

stages.prompt: What org design framework should guide your scaling plan?

options.label: Span of Control + Layer Analysis: Map optimal spans, add layer where >10 reports. Create new VP roles.
options.rationale: Correct first step. Before hiring, fix structure. Prevents flat-org chaos at 200 people.

options.label: Hire as fast as possible. Structure will sort itself out.
options.rationale: Recipe for chaos. No reporting clarity = decision paralysis and culture breakdown.

options.label: Implement matrix org with dotted lines to all VPs
options.rationale: Over-engineered for 200 people. Matrix orgs need strong PM culture and 500+ headcount to justify overhead.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain org design principles for scaling stages.

stages.prompt: VP Sales hiring has failed twice. Both candidates looked great on paper but quit within 60 days. Options:

options.label: Promote internal: top-performing rep with 3 yrs tenure, 180% quota. Give them 6-month trial as interim VP with outsourced coach. Hire strong #2.
options.rationale: Internal knows product/customers. Trial period derisks. Coach fills gaps. Better than empty seat for 9 months.

options.label: Hire external search firm, raise comp to 90th percentile, accept 3-month search timeline
options.rationale: Two failures suggest selection problem, not comp. 3 months empty = missed pipeline.

options.label: Merge Sales under VP Marketing. One fewer hire.
options.rationale: Different skill sets. Marketing lacks enterprise sales experience. Overloads existing leader.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate talent strategy trade-offs: speed vs. fit, internal vs. external, cost of vacancy.

stages.prompt: Two team managers showing burnout (weekend work, productivity drop). Team of 30 engineers depend on them. What do you do?

options.label: 1) Immediate: 2-week mandated PTO 2) Structural: Split each 15-person team into two 7-person teams with new managers promoted from within 3) Culture: Publicly model 'no weekend work' norm
options.rationale: Addresses root cause (oversized teams) while providing immediate relief. Models desired behavior.

options.label: Give them each a 20% raise and equity refresh. They deserve it for working hard.
options.rationale: Rewards harmful behavior. Burnout won't be solved by money. Reinforces 'martyr hero' culture.

options.label: Replace them. If they can't handle startup pace, find people who can.
options.rationale: Career-ending mistake. Top performers burning out = structural problem, not motivation problem. Replacing loses institutional knowledge.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain burnout prevention and team scaling principles.

optimal.title: Scaled Strong
optimal.description: 200 people in 18 months. Culture preserved. eNPS climbed to 85. Attrition under 8%. IPO-ready org.

acceptable.title: Growing Pains
acceptable.description: 165 people in 18 months (missed target). Some culture erosion in middle layers. Attrition 15%. Correctable.

failure.title: Culture Collapse
failure.description: Both managers left. VP Sales still empty. 35% attrition. eNPS dropped to 35. Series B runway wasted on recruiting churn.

title: Platform vs Feature Investment
description: Your CTO wants 6 months for a platform rewrite. Your VP Product wants to ship 3 new features that paying customers are asking for. You have 40 engineers.

context.company: B2B SaaS, $15M ARR, 40 engineers, monolithic Rails app
context.situation: CTO: 'Tech debt is slowing us down. Deploy frequency dropped from daily to weekly. 30% of sprint capacity on bug fixes. We need 6 months to extract core services.' VP Product: '3 enterprise logos ($5M ARR) require SSO, audit logs, and custom reporting to close. Miss these and we miss Q4 targets.'
context.time_pressure: Q4 planning meeting in 3 days. Engineering morale dropping. Customer escalations up.
data_provided: DORA metrics: Deploy freq 1/week (down from daily), Lead time 5 days, CFR 18% (up from 8%), MTTR 4 hours
Engineering morale: 45 eNPS (down from 72), 3 regrettable losses this quarter
Customer pipeline: 3 deals worth $5M ARR blocked by missing features
Platform scope: 6 months, $2M eng cost, projected 3x velocity after
Feature scope: 2 months each, $600k eng cost, unlocks $5M ARR

stages.prompt: Apply the Tech Debt Quadrant. What kind of debt is this?

options.label: Prudent-Deliberate: Original decisions were reasonable at the time. Now constraints changed and the architecture no longer fits.
options.rationale: Rails monolith was correct for first 5 years. At $15M ARR with enterprise customers, the architecture needs to evolve.

options.label: Reckless-Deliberate: CTO knowingly cut corners to ship faster.
options.rationale: No evidence of corner-cutting. Monolith was the right architecture at $1-5M ARR. Context changed.

options.label: Not tech debt - it's feature requests. Ship the features.
options.rationale: DORA metrics deterioration is real tech debt. 18% CFR means 1 in 5 deployments breaks something. Unsustainable.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain the tech debt quadrant and appropriate response per quadrant.

stages.prompt: With 40 engineers, how do you allocate?

options.label: 70/30 split: 28 engineers on features (SSO, audit, custom reporting) targeting 2-month delivery. 12 engineers on platform (extract 2 core services). Review at 2 months.
options.rationale: Addresses both needs simultaneously. Features unblock revenue. Platform investment starts. 2-month review gates commitment.

options.label: 100% platform: Full rewrite for 6 months. No new features.
options.rationale: Loses $5M ARR deals. Customers leave. 6 months without customer value = morale collapse and churn.

options.label: 100% features: Ship all 3 features in 6 months (~13 engineers each). Ignore platform.
options.rationale: Tech debt compounds. 18% CFR will become 30%. Good engineers leave. Features eventually grind to halt.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain the dual-track approach: how to balance innovation and maintenance investment.

stages.prompt: Engineering morale (eNPS 45, 3 losses). What do you do about the team?

options.label: 1) Share the dual-track plan transparently 2) Give each track a strong TL with decision rights 3) Protect 'no-interrupt' deep work blocks 4) Commit to quarterly retro on approach
options.rationale: Transparent plan + autonomy + protected time + feedback loop. Addresses root causes: uncertainty, lack of agency, context switching.

options.label: Announce 'crunch mode' for next 3 months. Free dinner and Uber credits.
options.rationale: Perks don't fix burnout. Crunch mode accelerates attrition. Engineers with options will leave.

options.label: Hire 10 more engineers. More capacity = less pressure.
options.rationale: Brooks' Law: adding people to late projects makes them later. Onboarding load on current team. Doesn't fix root cause.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate engineering team health interventions.

optimal.title: Dual Track Success
optimal.description: 2 features shipped in 3 months ($5M ARR closed). 2 services extracted in 5 months. DORA back to elite. Morale recovered to 70 eNPS.

acceptable.title: Tense Balance
acceptable.description: 1 feature delayed. Platform 1 month behind. Morale stable at 55. Tension between product and platform ongoing. Revenue $3M.

failure.title: Engineer Exodus
failure.description: Crunch mode burned out 12 engineers. Platform stalled. Features buggy (CFR 25%). 3 enterprise deals lost. Rebuild from smaller team.

title: Root Cause: Customer Churn Spike
description: Monthly churn doubled from 3% to 6% in 30 days. No product changes, no pricing changes, no competitor launches. Find the root cause.

context.situation: Churn spiked from 3% to 6% last month. No obvious trigger: no product changes, no pricing changes, no competitor launch. Support tickets up 40%. NPS dropped from 45 to 28. Sales team reports longer close cycles. Engineering says 'no major outages.'
context.time_pressure: Board update in 5 days. If churn stays at 6%, $600k ARR at risk this quarter.
data_provided: Churn by segment: Enterprise (2% > 4%), Mid-market (3% > 5%), SMB (6% > 15%)
Support tickets: 'onboarding' issues up 80%, 'data import' up 50%
Onboarding time: 45 days (was 30 days) per new customer
Customer success team: same 4 people, caseload up from 50 to 75 accounts each
NPS verbatims: 'too hard to set up', 'took 2 months to go live', 'training was insufficient'

stages.prompt: Which cause analysis method should you apply FIRST to identify the root cause?

options.label: Fishbone Diagram + 5 Whys: Categorize causes (People, Process, Technology, Measurement), then drill into each with 5 Whys
options.rationale: Multi-factor problem (both segments and support data suggest multiple contributors). Fishbone organizes, 5 Whys drills.

options.label: Fire the Head of Customer Success. Churn is their job.
options.rationale: Blaming before understanding = toxic culture + wrong fix. Data suggests systemic issue, not individual.

options.label: Run an A/B test on different onboarding flows
options.rationale: Too slow for 6% monthly churn. Need diagnosis before treatment. A/B test takes 2-3 months.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Explain which cause analysis method fits this problem type.

stages.prompt: Apply the Fishbone. Categorize the data into People, Process, Technology, and Measurement buckets. What pattern emerges?
stages.feedback_prompt_template: User analyzed {response}. Pattern: Process (onboarding stretched from 30 to 45 days because caseload doubled) and Measurement (no leading indicator for churn - only caught at cancellation). Root cause: Customer Success team didn't scale with customer growth. Caseload 50 > 75 = 50% increase in accounts per CSM. Onboarding time degradation directly correlates with churn spike.
stages.sample_answer: Process (onboarding stretched from 30 to 45 days because caseload doubled) and Measurement (no leading indicator for churn - only caught at cancellation).

stages.prompt: Given root cause is CS team overloaded (not scaled with growth). Choose your action:

options.label: 1) Immediate: Hire 2 CSMs, reduce caseload to 50 2) Process: Implement onboarding automation (self-service portal, email sequences) for first 14 days 3) Measurement: Add 'time-to-first-value' and 'onboarding completion' as leading churn indicators
options.rationale: Addresses all three levels: capacity (hire), efficiency (automate), monitoring (metrics). Systemic fix.

options.label: Just hire 4 more CSMs. More people = problem solved.
options.rationale: Capacity fix but no process improvement. Same problem at next growth stage. Hiring lag = continued churn.

options.label: Offer 20% discount to at-risk customers. Buy time.
options.rationale: Treats symptom (churn) not cause (poor onboarding). Revenue loss + same problem persists. Customers leave anyway.

stages.feedback_prompt_template: User chose {option}. Evaluate systemic vs symptomatic solutions to root cause.

optimal.title: Root Cause Fixed
optimal.description: Caseload reduced to 50. Onboarding automated for first 14 days. Time-to-value dropped to 25 days. Churn back to 3% in 3 months. Leading indicators now caught early.

acceptable.title: Symptom Managed
acceptable.description: Hired 2 CSMs but onboarding still manual. Churn dropped to 4% (not 3%). Process debt accumulating. Same problem at 800 customers.

failure.title: Spiral Continues
failure.description: Discounted churning customers. They left anyway after discount period. CS team burned out (2 quit). Churn hit 8%. ARR declining.
